Stage-1 mechanism is now backed by external manufacturer literature (see evidence) but not yet by an ELIMFILTERS-controlled document. FUEL_CANONICAL_GOVERNANCE.md treats a single external manufacturer source as internal evidence only; operator decides whether that is enough to publish the qualitative mechanism (no brand, no numbers).

evidence.use: internal evidence only; never cited or named on public surfaces
evidence.source: Parker Hannifin, Racor Division: Turbine Series 900FH/1000FH instruction sheet 12960 Rev D
evidence.finding: Stage 1 separation: incoming fuel passes through a centrifuge that spins off large solids and water droplets, which fall to the bottom of the collection bowl. Stage 2: fine droplets coalesce on a conical baffle and the cartridge. Stage 3: the cartridge captures fine contaminants.
evidence.retrieved: 2026-10-14 via web search summary; direct PDF fetch blocked from the build environment

evidence.source: Parker Hannifin, Racor Division: 500FG Turbine Series instruction sheet 15332
evidence.finding: The turbine is fixed: it uses the fuel's own flow to remove large solids and free water by centrifugal force. The figure was corrected to show a static deflector.

decisions.decision: Operator confirmed the TURBOCORE stage-1 mechanism: a turbine deflector centrifuges the fuel. Copy restored to state it. Attach an ELIMFILTERS-controlled document reference before publication (FUEL_CANONICAL_GOVERNANCE.md, claims blocked by default).
Readouts show qualitative states instead of numbers on both figures.
Look up the mechanism in Parker Hannifin literature. Result recorded as internal evidence; deflector animation changed from rotating to fixed to match it.

HYDROCORE is shown in its two differentiating configurations: spin-on with integrated drain (water settles in the cartridge sump; the whole cartridge is replaced at service) and separator with a reusable bowl (only the element is changed; the same bowl is refitted).

Add the third HYDROCORE configuration: replaceable separator elements that go inside permanent separator housings (not turbine housings); at service the bowl comes off, the element is changed and the same bowl is refitted. Show solid residues settling with the water in all fuel figures. TURBOCORE stays one figure; the fuel's swirl under the fixed deflector is shown with animated rings.

Operator shared field references (a HYDROCORE fuel filter / water separator photographed in service, and the ET97784 assembly render). Fig 1C redrawn to match: metal shroud under the head, tall transparent bowl with the pleated element visible inside, red seal at the rim and drain at the bottom; service takes the bowl off, changes the element and refits the same bowl. Label text, micron ratings and addresses on the references are not reproduced.

ET97784 is sold as one complete assembly (head, spin-on element, bowl and drain), so it carries the assembly prefix ET9 / TURBOCORE on its label; its replaceable service element ES91434 stays ES9 / HYDROCORE. The figures keep showing the separator mechanism as HYDROCORE (ES9) and do not reproduce product labels.

The three HYDROCORE figures are approved at illustrative level and published in the Knowledge Center technology page (How It Works), because they explain how the technology works. English builds (--en) are served from frontend/public/knowledge-center/figures and linked from preview cards; the site's frame policy (X-Frame-Options DENY) is left unchanged.
